page.title: Tutorial · tinyactors CLI
page.description: Compile an order chart, fix a misspelt timeout with tinyactors lint, trace the path to shipped and run an order session.

hero.headline: Compile, lint, draw and run an order chart
hero.lede: In seven commands, you compile an order chart and catch a misspelt timeout event with lint, without running it. After the fix, a scripted session retries an unanswered charge after 30 seconds and ends in paid.

section.heading: 1. Compile the order chart
section.p: Your order chart collects items, starts checkout and requests a charge. When the payment service does not answer within 30 seconds, it tries up to three times.
Save this chart as order.scxml and run tinyactors compile to build order.tai for your application. The chart compiles with zero diagnostics.

section.heading: 2. Catch unhandled events with lint
section.p: Valid syntax does not guarantee your order can finish. Run tinyactors lint to inspect the chart's transition logic without executing it.

The output reports an unhandled-event warning because paying sends payment.timeout while its transitions expect payment.timedout. Without a matching transition, an order whose payment service never answers waits forever.

section.heading: 3. Fix the event and check again
section.p: Update both transitions in paying from payment.timedout to payment.timeout. That fixes both the retry transition and the final cancellation after three attempts.
Next, run check -W to validate the chart without writing an output file. Because -W turns warnings into errors, seeing Valid: yes confirms no errors or warnings remain.
Now run lint --deny all so any remaining finding fails with exit code 1. This time lint finds nothing and exits with 0.

section.heading: 4. Trace the path to shipped
section.p: Check that your order can reach shipped by running tinyactors path from open. The command lists three transitions and notes that checkout requires total > 0.

section.heading: 5. Draw the order chart
section.p: Run graph -f svg to inspect your order flow as state boxes and labelled routes. The resulting SVG follows your system's light or dark setting.

drawing.alt: The order chart showing open, paying, paid, shipped and cancelled, with paying's retry looping back to itself

section.heading: 6. Run an order session
section.p: To test the retry flow, pipe JSON-RPC requests into tinyactors run, one request per line. This script adds a pen, checks out, lets 30 seconds pass and answers the second charge.
Passing --io-processor payments lets your session act as the payment service. Each effect.send notification represents a charge request from your order.
After request 5 advances the clock 30 seconds, request 6 fires your fixed timeout and emits a second charge. Request 9 shows the order in paid.

section.heading: Put the checks in your build
section.p: Once your chart works locally, run these checks in CI to catch mistakes before a pull request merges. Pair check and lint with fmt and diff, or drive sessions from a script.

item.text: Automate check, lint, fmt and diff on every pull request.
